newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: GP Batteries to raise S$42 mln in issue.
newsitem.headline: GP Batteries to raise S$42 mln in issue.

text.p: GP Batteries International Ltd, the Singapore-listed subsidiary of Hong Kong Gold Peak Industries (Holdings) Ltd, said on Thursday it hoped to raise Singapore $41.92 million in a 10 million share offer.
The company is offering about the shares at S$4.43 each, a figure based on the last transacted price of S$4.62 per share on June 12, 1997 less a discount of 4.1 per cent.
It said in a statement, S$31 million of the net proceeds would be due to GP Batteries and S$10.92 million to Gold Peak.

GP Batteries chairman Andrew Ng was quoted as saying about S$10 million would be used for expansion of existing business and development of new products and S$8 million to buy machinery and equipment. The rest would be used as working capital.

With the issue of new GP Batteries shares, Gold Peak's shareholding in GP Batteries will drop to 45.3 percent from 50.1 percent, making GP Batteries its associated company instead of a major subsidiary.
DBS and Peregrine were appointed placement agents for the share offer.
After the share issue, GP Batteries issued and paid-up capital will be increased to S$74.8 million from S$69.2 million.
Its net asset backing per share will be increased to S$2.05 from S$1.86 and gearing will fall to 45.7 percent from 62 percent.
